data.name: Homer
data.gender_notes: Homer is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Ὅμηρος (Homeros), which is composed of the elements ὅμηρ (homēr), meaning 'host' or 'comrade', and -os, a suffix denoting 'man' or 'sweller'. Homer is revered in Greek mythology as the legendary poet who authored the Iliad and the Odyssey. The name Homer carries the meaning “Wise,al, Comrade” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Homer usually hope their child will grow to embody wise,al, comrade and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, companionship, and poetic storytelling.
data.etymology: Homer belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise,al, Comrade.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Homer total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_greek.name: Όμηρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Όμηρος είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την αρχαία Ελλάδα και σημαίνει προστάτης ή όμηρος. Στο πλαίσιο της χριστιανικής παράδοσης, το όνομα αυτό δεν έχει άμεση σχέση με το θρήσκευμα, αλλά έχει ιστορική σημασία ως όνομα του περίφημου ποιητή της Ιλιάδας και της Οδύσσειας.

in_english.name: Homer
in_english.meaning: Homer means hostage or pledge, a devoted follower
in_english.long_meaning: The name Homer originates from ancient Greek roots, specifically from 'Όμηρος' (Homerus in Latin), meaning hostage or pledge. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, Homer has been adopted in Christian contexts as a given name, symbolizing devotion or a pledge of faith. Historically, it is associated with the legendary poet of the Iliad and Odyssey. The name Homer conveys a sense of loyalty and dedication, traits valued in Christian tradition.
